items.rationale: The message history lives in the program and ends with the session; nothing was written to storage, so the Wednesday call started empty. Choosing a or d shows the belief that the model keeps its own memory between sessions.

Each call re-sends the whole history. Call 1 sends 1,000 + 100 = 1,100; call 2 adds 500 for 1,600; call 3 adds another 500 for 2,100. The total is 1,100 + 1,600 + 2,100 = 4,800. An answer of 2,100 counts only the last call; 2,600 counts only new text.

Search runs in the program over an index, and only the returned chunks are added to the history. The model never sees the rest of the manual, so retrieval quality decides what it can use. Choosing b shows the belief that the model reads the whole manual.
Compaction summarizes a conversation near the limit and restarts a fresh window with the summary, trading detail for space.

The memory tool is client-side: the model requests a file operation like any tool call, and your application performs it and returns the result. Choosing b shows the belief that the model stores things itself.
